note: R25: ninth hand-written set, untouched test for one pre-registered comparison, written without access to the frozen test

stories.text: Deep under the hill at Brannock Farm, the cheesemaker, Wendeline Ferrand, turned the wheels of cheese every morning. Her apprentice, a quiet boy named Mawuli, brushed salt water onto the rinds. On Thursday a buyer from the city tasted a slice and ordered twelve wheels. They were wrapped in waxed cloth and loaded onto a van before dark.
qs: Who turned the wheels of cheese every morning?
What did Mawuli brush onto the rinds?
How many wheels did the buyer order?
What were the wheels wrapped in?

stories.text: A badger called Brackwell dug a new burrow under a hawthorn hedge. Before he had finished, a family of rabbits moved into the front room and refused to leave. Brackwell did not argue with them. Instead he dug a second door at the back, and that winter the rabbits kept the front of the burrow warm while he slept snugly at the far end.
qs: Where did Brackwell dig the burrow?
Who moved into the front room?
What did Brackwell dig at the back?
What did the rabbits keep warm?

stories.text: The mountain bus left Vellara at six in the morning with eleven passengers. Its driver, Mr Saito, stopped at the dairy halfway up to collect the milk churns. At the pass a hiker named Sigrun got off with her map, and the bus went down the far side to the market town of Ostrell. By noon the churns had been unloaded, and Mr Saito was drinking coffee in the square.
qs: When did the bus leave Vellara?
What did the driver collect at the dairy?
Where was Mr Saito at noon?

stories.text: Mrs Ndukwe carried her husband's old boots to the cobbler's in Tannerby. The cobbler, a tall man named Cathal, found that both soles had worn through. He stitched new leather soles onto them while she waited, and he polished the toes until they shone. She paid him four coins and wrapped the boots in brown paper for the walk home.
qs: Who carried the boots to the cobbler's?
Who stitched new soles onto the boots?
What did Mrs Ndukwe wrap the boots in?

stories.text: In a dry summer a tortoise named Pembe found the last puddle in the valley. A proud stork, Altair, said the water was his because he had seen it first from the sky. Pembe answered that the sky did not drink. While they argued, the sun dried the puddle, and both of them had to walk to the river after all.
qs: Who found the last puddle in the valley?
Who said the water was his?
Why did the stork say the water was his?
Where did both of them have to walk?

stories.text: Every morning at seven, Dr Rasmusdottir climbed the path from the village to the weather station above Skarvik. There she read the rain gauge and wrote the numbers in a green notebook. At ten a radio call came from the harbour master, Gergely, who wanted to know about the wind. She told him a storm was coming, so he kept the fishing boats in port, and in the afternoon she walked back down to the village.
qs: Who climbed the path to the weather station?
Where did Dr Rasmusdottir write the numbers?
When did the radio call come?
Who wanted to know about the wind?
Where did Dr Rasmusdottir walk in the afternoon?

stories.text: In the square at Hembury there is a hat shop run by two sisters, Esmeralda and Amparo Quirino. Esmeralda steams the felt and shapes it on wooden blocks, while Amparo sews the ribbons on. Last week a bride's mother ordered a wide blue hat for the wedding. The hat was finished on Friday, and the shop boy, Hipolito, delivered it in a round box.
qs: What did the bride's mother order?

stories.text: A young otter, Sisu, was afraid of the deep pool below the weir. Each evening his grandmother floated on her back near the bank and called to him. One night a heron stood on the bank where Sisu usually sat, so he slipped into the water to get away from it. By morning he was swimming beside his grandmother as if he had never been afraid.
qs: Who was afraid of the deep pool?
What did his grandmother do each evening?
What stood on the bank where Sisu usually sat?
Why did Sisu slip into the water?

stories.text: The cafe at the end of Sandle Pier opens at dawn for the fishermen. Its owner, Rasha, bakes bread rolls in the back kitchen before anyone arrives. At midday the tourists come off the ferry, and her nephew Isandro carries trays out to the tables on the deck. In the evening the chairs are stacked inside and the shutters are locked.
qs: Where does Rasha bake the rolls?
When do the tourists come off the ferry?
Who carries trays out to the tables?
What are stacked inside in the evening?

stories.text: Mr Uzoma grows young oak and birch trees at a forest nursery outside Lindqvarn. In April his daughter, Chidinma, planted three hundred acorns in a shaded bed by the stream. The seedlings came up in May, and a man from the council came to count them. In autumn they were dug up and taken to the burnt hillside, where volunteers planted them in the rain.
qs: Who grows young oak and birch trees?
Where did Chidinma plant the acorns?
Who came to count the seedlings?
Where were the seedlings taken in autumn?

stories.text: A crow named Ebon collected shiny buttons and kept them in a nest at the top of a chimney. When the family below lit their first fire of the year, smoke poured up through the nest. Ebon flew out coughing, and the buttons fell down the chimney into the hearth. The little girl of the house, Freya, found them in the ashes and sewed them onto her coat.
qs: What poured up through the nest?
Where did Freya find the buttons?
What did Freya do with the buttons?

stories.text: Early on Monday the sailmaker, Ambrose Nkemelu, unrolled a torn mainsail across the floor of the sail loft. He had fetched it the evening before from the yacht Merrow, which was tied up in the marina. All morning he stitched a canvas patch over the tear with a curved needle. At three o'clock his assistant, Clea, rowed the sail back out to the yacht.
qs: What did the sailmaker unroll across the floor?
Where was the yacht tied up?
What did he stitch over the tear?
When did Clea row the sail back to the yacht?
Who rowed the sail back out to the yacht?

stories.text: Old Mr Fitzgibbon could no longer reach the apples on his tallest tree. His neighbour, a nurse called Divya, brought a ladder over the fence one Saturday. While she picked, he held the basket steady, and her two sons carried the full baskets to his shed. In return he gave them a jar of apple jelly every week until Christmas.
qs: What could Mr Fitzgibbon no longer reach?
Who brought a ladder over the fence?
What did Mr Fitzgibbon hold steady?
Who carried the full baskets to his shed?
What did he give them every week?

stories.text: Two squirrels, Kestrin and Moll, shared an old elm at the edge of the park. Kestrin hid his nuts in a hundred places and forgot most of them, while Moll kept hers in one hole in the trunk. One winter a woodpecker drilled into the trunk and ate everything in Moll's hole. That spring Kestrin shared the few nuts he could still find, and his forgotten ones grew into young trees all over the park.
qs: Who hid his nuts in a hundred places?
Where did Moll keep her nuts?
Whose hole did the woodpecker empty?
What did the forgotten nuts grow into?

stories.text: On Saturday the Monteiro family left their flat in the city and drove to the lake. At the boathouse they hired a rowing boat, and Ernesto, the eldest, rowed them across to a small island. They ate lunch under a willow there while their dog, Bosun, chased ducks along the shore. In the evening they rowed back, returned the boat, and drove home in the dark.
qs: Where did the family hire a rowing boat?
Who rowed them across to the island?
What did Bosun chase along the shore?

stories.text: A library van that visits the hill villages broke down near Ashcombe on Tuesday. Its driver, Mrs Stavrou, telephoned the garage, and a mechanic named Esteban arrived within the hour. While he mended the fan belt, she lent books to the children who had gathered round. The van reached its last village two hours late, but nobody seemed to mind.
qs: What did Mrs Stavrou do while he worked?
When did the van break down?

stories.text: A field mouse named Tansy lived beneath a scarecrow in a wheat field. Every year the farmer replaced the scarecrow's straw, and every year Tansy lined her nest with the old straw. One autumn the farmer brought a cat instead of new straw. That night Tansy packed her seeds into the scarecrow's hat and moved to the hedge, where the cat never thought to look.
qs: What did Tansy line her nest with?
What did the farmer bring instead of new straw?
Where did Tansy pack her seeds?

stories.text: At eight the post van dropped three sacks at the village shop in Tregarth. The postwoman, Dobrawa, sorted the letters on the counter and set off on her bicycle. She went first to the farms along the river, then up to the vicarage, and she ate her sandwiches on the bench by the war memorial. By four o'clock her bag was empty and her bicycle was back in the shed behind the shop.
qs: When did the post van drop the sacks?
What did Dobrawa set off on?
Where did she eat her sandwiches?
Where was her bicycle by four o'clock?

stories.text: Ms Horvath teaches music at the school in Wrexley. Before the spring concert she lent her own violin to a pupil, Chukwudi, because his had a cracked neck. The cracked one was sent to a repairer in town, who glued it and fitted new strings. On the night of the concert Chukwudi played a solo, and his grandparents clapped from the front row.
qs: Who teaches music at the school?
Who did Ms Horvath lend her violin to?
Why did Ms Horvath lend her violin?
What did Chukwudi play on the night of the concert?
Who clapped from the front row?

stories.text: A goat named Brimble and a donkey named Osk shared a field behind the farmhouse. When the gate blew open in a gale, the goat wanted to run to the cabbage garden, but the donkey said the road was dangerous. The goat went alone and was chased all the way back by the farm dog, Sabre. After that Brimble listened when Osk spoke, and Osk let him stand on his back to reach the apple branches.
qs: Where did the goat want to run?
Who said the road was dangerous?
What did Osk let Brimble do?

stories.text: On Wednesday morning Mr Abernathy's class took the train from Corrin to the coast. They spent the morning at the tide pools, where a ranger named Nasrin showed them starfish and crabs. After lunch they visited the lighthouse and climbed its hundred and twelve steps. The train brought them home at six, and parents were waiting on the platform.
qs: Whose class took the train to the coast?
Where did the class spend the morning?
Who showed them starfish and crabs?
What did they visit after lunch?
What did they climb at the lighthouse?

stories.text: At the Pewter Jug cafe the cook, Vojtech, starts the soup at five in the morning. His sister Zelda takes the orders and writes them on a slate. On Sundays the cafe is closed, so Vojtech goes fishing on the reservoir with his friend Okello. Whatever they catch is cooked for Monday's lunch.
qs: When does Vojtech start the soup?
Who writes the orders on a slate?
What does Zelda write the orders on?

stories.text: A snail named Pellam decided to visit his cousin on the far side of the garden path. A blackbird, Merle, offered to carry him in her beak, but Pellam did not trust her. He crossed the path slowly through a whole afternoon, and the blackbird kept watch so that no thrush could reach him. When he arrived he thanked her, and the two have been friends ever since.
qs: Who decided to visit his cousin?
What did Merle offer to carry him in?
How long did Pellam take to cross the path?

stories.text: Captain Kabongo's ferry left Tarbet harbour at nine with a cargo of flour and two cars. Halfway across the sound the fog came down, and she slowed the engines and sounded the horn. The ferry reached the island an hour late, where young Rhodri was waiting on the slipway with a tractor. By the afternoon the flour was in the island bakery and the ferry was on its way back.
qs: When did the ferry leave the harbour?
What came down halfway across the sound?
Who was waiting on the slipway?
Where was the flour by the afternoon?

stories.text: Every year the residents of Thimble Court sign a card for their caretaker, Mr Zungu. This year Mrs Holloway took the card from door to door, and forty neighbours signed it in the hallway. The children drew a picture of his red toolbox on the back. On his birthday they left it on his desk in the boiler room, with a cake from the corner bakery.
qs: What did the residents sign for their caretaker?
Who took the card from door to door?
Where did the neighbours sign the card?
How many neighbours signed the card?
Where did they leave the card?

stories.text: A frog named Bulmer lived in a rain barrel behind a greenhouse. Every night he sang so loudly that the gardener's cat, Pashmina, could not sleep. The cat complained to the moths, and the moths complained to the moon, but nobody could stop the frog. In the end a dry week quieted him, because the barrel ran low and he went off to find a pond.
qs: Who did the cat complain to?
What quieted the frog in the end?
Why did Bulmer go off to find a pond?

stories.text: On the morning of the fair, Grandpa Anand packed his jars of honey into a wooden crate. His granddaughter, Golnar, carried the crate to the car while he locked the hives. They drove to the fairground at Wetherby Green and set up a table beside the cider tent. Golnar watched the stall at lunchtime while her grandfather walked round the show ring, and by evening every jar was sold.
qs: Where did Grandpa Anand pack his jars of honey?
Who carried the crate to the car?
When did Golnar watch the stall?
Where did her grandfather walk at lunchtime?

stories.text: Dr Ngata is the only vet on the island of Skerra. When a ewe at Hollins Farm had trouble with her lamb, the farmer, Ciaran, phoned her at midnight. She drove across the island in her old jeep and helped the lamb into the world. The farmer's wife made her tea in the kitchen, and the lamb was named Midnight.
qs: Who is the only vet on the island?
When did Ciaran phone the vet?
How did Dr Ngata cross the island?
What did Dr Ngata help into the world?

stories.text: A young fox, Rufina, wanted to learn to climb like the cats in the village. Each night she practised on the woodpile behind the inn, and each night she fell off. The innkeeper's old tomcat, Barnaby, watched her from the windowsill and finally came down to show her how to use her claws. By midsummer she could reach the roof of the woodshed, though she never did learn to come down gracefully.
qs: Who wanted to learn to climb?
Who watched her from the windowsill?
What did Barnaby show her how to use?
When could she reach the roof of the woodshed?

stories.text: On Monday a parcel of rare seeds left a seed bank in the north and travelled by train to the capital. On Tuesday it was flown to a mountain town, and a courier named Dawit carried it by motorbike to the research garden. There the head gardener, Mrs Llewellyn, signed for the parcel at the gate. By Friday the seeds were planted in the glasshouse, each in its own labelled pot.
qs: How did the parcel travel to the capital?
Who carried the parcel by motorbike?
Where did Mrs Llewellyn sign for the parcel?

stories.text: The clock on the bus station in Dunmarra stopped at twenty past four one windy night. In the morning the town clerk, Ms Akinyemi, sent for a clockmaker, Mr Bergkvist, who arrived on the noon bus. He climbed the ladder inside the tower and found that a pigeon had built a nest against the hands. He moved the nest to a box on the roof, oiled the gears, and the clock was going again by tea time.
qs: Who arrived on the noon bus?
What had built a nest against the hands?

stories.text: A beaver named Osgood built a dam that turned the meadow into a pond. The moorhens loved the pond, but an old vole, Hepzibah, grumbled because her tunnels had flooded. Osgood felt sorry for her and built her a dry room in the side of his lodge. Now the vole sleeps above the water and the moorhens nest in the reeds outside.
qs: What did the dam turn the meadow into?

stories.text: At dawn the herder, Batzorig, drove his goats from the village to the high pasture. He spent the day on a rock above the stream, carving a spoon and watching for wolves. When the sun dropped behind the ridge, he whistled for his dog and brought the goats down again. By nightfall the goats were in their pen behind the house, and Batzorig was eating noodles by the stove.
qs: Where did Batzorig drive his goats at dawn?
Where were the goats by nightfall?
What was Batzorig doing by the stove?

stories.text: The footbridge over the river in Kilnsey was painted by volunteers last weekend. The paint was donated by a hardware shop owned by Mr Banerjee, and the brushes were lent by the primary school. A retired engineer, Mrs Adewale, checked every bolt before the painting began. The work was finished on Sunday afternoon, and the bridge is now bright green.
qs: What was lent by the primary school?

stories.text: On the roof of the railway station lived two pigeons, Vesper and Cobble. Vesper boasted that she could fly to the next town faster than the express train. Cobble did not believe her, so they agreed on a race the next morning. Vesper flew straight, but a gust blew her into a church tower, and Cobble, who had ridden on the roof of the train, was waiting for her on the platform.
qs: Who boasted she could fly faster than the train?
What blew Vesper into a church tower?
How did Cobble get to the next town?

stories.text: Each Saturday Mrs Tembo takes the early boat from her island to the mainland market. She sells woven baskets from a stall under the clock tower until the church bells ring at one. Then she buys rice, lamp oil and a newspaper, and she meets her son, Chilufya, for lunch at a cafe on the quay. The last boat carries her home at five.
qs: Who takes the early boat to the mainland?
Who does she meet for lunch?
When does the last boat carry her home?

stories.text: Captain Ngcobo, who retired from the sea last year, now builds model ships in his garage. His granddaughter, Ayodele, paints the tiny flags, and his dog sleeps under the workbench. This spring one of his models, a three-masted schooner, won first prize at the county show. The judges asked where he had learned to tie such small knots, and he said he had learned on a real ship long ago.
qs: Where does Captain Ngcobo build model ships?
What did Captain Ngcobo retire from?
What won first prize at the county show?

stories.text: A spider called Nettlewick spun her web across the window of a garden shed. A clumsy bumblebee, Barrow, flew into it twice in one morning and tore it both times. The spider was angry at first, but she noticed that the bee always came from the lavender. She moved her web to the other window, and after that the two of them never troubled each other again.
qs: Who spun a web across the window of a garden shed?
How many times did the bee fly into the web?
Where did the spider move her web?

stories.text: On Monday morning a child's red mitten was dropped on the tram. The conductor, Hildegard, found it under a seat and took it to the lost property office at the depot. On Wednesday a woman named Mrs Villaverde came to the depot asking for a mitten, and the clerk gave it back to her. That evening the mitten was back on her daughter's hand at the skating rink.
qs: What was dropped on the tram?
Who came to the depot asking for a mitten?
Where was the mitten that evening?

stories.text: Przemek cut his knee on a rock while he was crabbing with his cousin, Leilani, on Saturday. She helped him limp to the small clinic by the harbour, where Dr Rahimi stitched the cut. The doctor wrapped the knee in a white bandage and told him to keep it dry for a week. Przemek spent Sunday on the sofa, reading comics his cousin had brought from the shop.
qs: What did Przemek cut on a rock?
Who helped Przemek limp to the clinic?
What did the doctor wrap the knee in?
